translations.source_sense_description: eine tragbare Kopie eines Zeichens, eines grafischen Symbols

glosses: A distinctive mark, token, sign, emblem or cognizance, worn on one’s clothing, as an insignia of some rank, or of the membership of an organization.

examples.text: Tax-gatherers, […]recognized by their official badges.
the badge of a society; the badge of a policeman

glosses: A small nameplate, identifying the wearer, and often giving additional information.
A card, sometimes with a barcode or magnetic strip, granting access to a certain area.
Something characteristic; a mark; a token.

examples.text: Sweet mercy is nobility’s true badge.

glosses: A brand on the hand of a thief, etc.

examples.text: He has got his badge, and piked.
examples.translation: He was branded on the hand, and is at liberty.
examples.english: He was branded on the hand, and is at liberty.

glosses: A carved ornament on the stern of a vessel, containing a window or the representation of one.
A distinctive mark worn by servants, retainers, and followers of royalty or nobility, who, being beneath the rank of gentlemen, have no right to armorial bearings.
A small overlay on an icon that shows additional information about that item, such as the number of new alerts or messages.
An icon or emblem awarded to a user for some achievement.

examples.text: When you have checked in to the site from ten different cities, you unlock the Traveller badge.

glosses: A police officer.

examples.text: That's why every badge back home wanted to nail him.

glosses: To mark or distinguish with a badge.

examples.text: The television was badged as ‘GE’, but wasn’t made by them.

glosses: To show a badge to.

examples.text: He calmed down a lot when the policeman badged him.

glosses: To enter a restricted area by showing one’s badge.

examples.text: Worden and James walk […] to the […] Courthouse […], where they badge their way past sheriff’s deputies and take the elevator to the third floor.

And Patterson didn’t hear that Jack Egger, the studio’s director of security, said he’d seen John Orr badge his way through the pedestrian gate sometime before 4:00 pm, when the fire was still raging, […]
Our regional commissioner, his assistant commissioner and our district director, along with their wives, were hoofing it to the rotunda. Apparently they didn’t try and badge their way through.
Aaron badged into the data center and escorted Geoff inside the large room with its many blinking green lights.

examples.text: Comment ne sentez-vous pas que faire une scène sans preuves suffisantes, à M. Valenod, est la plus insigne des maladresses ?

glosses: Qui s’impose ; que l’on met en valeur.

examples.text: Le président du Brésil, à qui revenait l’insigne honneur de prononcer le premier discours de la session, est alors en grande forme.

glosses: Il se prend en mauvaise part, en parlant des choses et des personnes.

examples.text: Au Tchad, nous changerons nos chevaux de réquisition (qui sont d’insignes rosses) et nos bêtes de somme contre des chameaux pour continuer notre route dans la zone désertique d'Agadem.

glosses: Marque distinctive d’un grade, d’une dignité.
target_senses.note: Il s’emploie dans cette acception le plus souvent au pluriel

examples.text: Chaque année, les chanoinesses élisaient entre elles la bâtonnière, dont les fonctions consistaient à porter les insignes du chapitre noble, dans les processions générales et à l’inauguration du souverain.

glosses: Ce qui sert à distinguer les membres de tel ou tel groupement.

examples.text: Acceptons que le courage militaire demeure l’apanage d’une caste enfantine et bruyante, et ne se répande pas, comme l’a fait la Légion d’honneur, son insigne, parmi les professeurs, les contrôleurs, les peintres…
Bientôt, Bert fit l’emplette d’un complet de cycliste, avec la casquette, l’insigne et tous les accessoires.
